contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok (UpdateResult) on success; 404 when the collection is missing; 400 on an invalid filter
contract_grounding.note: assertion_text_quoted is the verbatim description field of qdrant_behavioral_points_delete_001 in structured_contract.json; the same assertion object also carries expected_behavior: "valid delete returns HTTP 200; missing collection returns 404; malformed filter returns 400" (recorded here in note, not inside the quote, to keep the quote a pure verbatim substring). The observed values (filter.should=null, and a must condition {"key":"grp"} with no matcher) sit inside the quoted constraint's own filter-clause domain and were accepted with 200+success, while the same server rejects sibling malformed filter shapes with exactly 400 (m1/m4/B5) — so violates=true is honest, not conservative drift. Caveat for the auditor: the 400 branch is not page-verbatim prose (page documents only the 200 response); its anchors are the server's own sibling dispositions and the source's own validator text (validate_field_condition). source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST: actix delete_points (src/actix/api/update_api.rs:81, no validate) -> do_delete_points (src/common/update.rs:412, no validate) -> DeletePointsByFilter -> split_by_shard to_all (lib/collection/src/operations/point_ops.rs:73) -> per-shard delete with the filter evaluated per point. Deserialization: PointsSelector is #[serde(untagged)] (point_ops.rs:19-26); for m2, FilterSelector matches and Filter.should Option<Vec<Condition>> goes through MaybeOneOrMany whose .unit(|| Ok(None)) maps explicit JSON null to None (utils.rs:101-102, unit-tested at utils.rs:154-163) -> the resulting filter has every clause None, i.e. an empty filter, which matches all points -> wipe (count 3 -> 0), consistent with the contract doc_quote's documented 'whole-collection wipe if the filter matches all' semantics for delete-by-filter. For m3, Condition is untagged (types.rs:3390-3403) and Field(FieldCondition) accepts {"key":"grp"} since every matcher is Option (types.rs:3040-3067). The codebase's own validator validate_field_condition (types.rs:3232-3240, 'At least one field condition must be specified') plus Filter's #[validate(nested)] would produce exactly the promised 400 — but no .validate() is invoked anywhere on the REST delete path (checked src/actix/** and src/common/update.rs); the gRPC face does invoke request validation at entry (src/tonic/api/points_api.rs:95), a face asymmetry, though its generated FieldCondition lacks a validator derive so deep condition checking on gRPC is unproven. Live cross-face (gRPC) comparison unobtainable: TESTVDB_DB_URL not available to the builder — face_unavailable.
source_grounding.outcome_detail: Split verdict recorded honestly for the auditor: (a) m3 ({"key":"grp"}) — validation_absent on the REST path: the exact validator exists in source (validate_field_condition) but is never invoked by the actix delete_points -> do_delete_points chain, so the source does not perform the validation the contract requires on this face; no comment or maintainer marker declares the skip intentional. (b) m2 ({"should":null}) — the null->None normalization primitive is explicitly unit-tested intent (utils.rs test_deserialize_one_or_many asserts {"data": null} -> is_none()), and the subsequent wipe is empty-filter-matches-all semantics that the contract's verified doc_quote itself sanctions for delete-by-filter; this is recorded as a surviving by-design defense for the auditor to weigh rather than asserted as by_design_in_source, because no intent marker covers the delete endpoint's decision to skip validation itself. Overall verification_outcome=validation_absent refers to the tested REST face performing no post-deserialization request validation.
